title: Positive-power linearization of a relatively very ample line over an affine base
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $r\geq0$, and $C=A[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$. Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}C=\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$ [def-sc-gm-ga], where $C$ has $A$-basis $t^u$ for $u\in\mathbf Z^r$, $t^ut^v=t^{u+v}$, $\Delta(t^u)=t^u\otimes t^u$, $\varepsilon(t^u)=1$, and antipode $t^u\mapsto t^{-u}$. Assume $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $f:X\to S$ be separated and of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and suppose every local ring of $X$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $a:T\times_S X\to X$ be an $S$-action, with the unit and associativity identities as scheme-morphism equalities [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] relatively very ample over $S$ [def-trf-relatively-very-ample]. Then there exists an integer $m\geq1$ such that $L^{\otimes m}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] admits a $T$-linearization. A $T$-linearization of an invertible module $M$ means an isomorphism $\theta:p_2^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*M$ on $T\times_S X$ [def-pc-module-pullback], restricting to $1_M$ along the identity and satisfying $\theta_{gh,x}=\theta_{g,hx}\theta_{h,x}$ on $T\times_S T\times_S X$ as an equality of pulled-back sheaf maps. Empty or disconnected $X$, the zero ring, nonreduced $A$, and $r=0$ are allowed; normality is required of $X$, not of $S$.

source.place: WANTED local copy. R. W. Thomason, Equivariant resolution, linearization, and Hilbert's fourteenth problem over arbitrary base schemes, Adv. Math. 65 (1987), proof of Theorem 3.3, printed p.32, first paragraph: the positive-power linearization input before choosing a coherent submodule of sections. Read primary article online at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/243015730_Equivariant_resolution_linearization_and_Hilbert%27s_fourteenth_problem_over_arbitrary_base_schemes . This is the split-torus case of that input; no Stacks tag is asserted for this theorem.

proof.text: The single affine open $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a Noetherian affine cover, so $S$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Since $f$ is of finite type, it is locally of finite type; [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $X$ locally Noetherian. Its local rings are domains by the given normality. Write $q=p_2:T\times_SX\to X$ and $e_X(x)=(1,x)$. From the specified Laurent coordinate algebra, $T\times_SX$ is exactly the Laurent-space scheme $Y$ in the next input: over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$, the tensor product $C\otimes_A R$ has the basis $t^u$ and is $R[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$. The inverse coefficient maps send $t_i\otimes1$ to $t_i$ and $1\otimes b$ to $b$.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; the affine Laurent coordinate identification is by the given basis and tensor universal property.

proof.text: Pullback preserves invertibility: a rank-one frame pulls back to a rank-one frame because $\mathcal O_Y\otimes_{g^{-1}\mathcal O_X}g^{-1}\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback]. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-laurent-line-invariance] to $N=a^*L$ on $Y=T\times_SX$. All its hypotheses hold by step 1 and normality of $X$. The action unit $a e_X=1_X$ identifies $e_X^*a^*L$ with $L$, using the pullback composition isomorphisms. Thus its conclusion gives an isomorphism $\theta_0:q^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*L$.

proof.text: The restriction $\alpha=e_X^*\theta_0$ is an automorphism of $L$. Every endomorphism of a line is multiplication by a unique regular scalar: in a local frame it is multiplication by its value on that frame, and changing the frame by a unit leaves that scalar unchanged. Therefore the local scalars glue; for an automorphism they glue to a unit. Define $\theta=\theta_0\circ q^*(\alpha^{-1})$. Since $q e_X=1_X$, its restriction along $e_X$ is $\alpha\alpha^{-1}=1_L$. Pullbacks and compositions here are the tensor pullbacks of [def-pc-module-pullback]; the assertions can equally be checked in these local frames.

proof.text: On $T\times_ST\times_SX$, the two maps $\theta_{gh,x}$ and $\theta_{g,hx}\theta_{h,x}$ have the same source and target, by associativity of the action. Their ratio is an automorphism of a line, hence a unique global unit $d$ by the frame calculation of step 3. The identity restriction of $\theta$ gives $d(1,h,x)=1$ and $d(g,1,x)=1$ as equalities of regular functions on the two identity faces, not merely on geometric points. We prove that $d=1$ by the following local calculation.

source.place: Agent proof of the split-torus linearization input in Thomason, proof of Theorem 3.3, p.32; geometric input derived from Tags 0BD7 and 0BDA, with the normalized cocycle checked by finite Laurent supports.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and set $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, a domain. Pull $d$ and its inverse back to the Laurent scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}R$; write the resulting inverse Laurent polynomials as $P,Q$ in the $2r$ variables $g,h$. Order $\mathbf Z^{2r}$ lexicographically. For finite nonempty supports over a domain, the least (respectively greatest) exponent of a product is the sum of the least (respectively greatest) exponents: its coefficient is the product of the two extremal nonzero coefficients, since no other pair gives that extremum. Since $PQ=1$, their widths satisfy $(\max P-\min P)+(\max Q-\min Q)=0$. Both widths are nonnegative in this ordered group, so both are zero. Thus $P=cg^uh^v$ for a unit $c\in R^\times$. The face identities say $ch^v=1$ and $cg^u=1$; uniqueness of Laurent coefficients forces $c=1$ and $u=v=0$. Consequently $P=1$. On any affine open $U\subseteq X$, expand $d-1$ in Laurent monomials. Each coefficient has zero germ at every $x\in U$ by this calculation, so it is zero by the sheaf axiom. Thus $d=1$ on the opens $T^2\times_SU$ covering $T^2\times_SX$. This proves the required cocycle. When $r=0$ the exponent group is zero and the same calculation applies. The argument is local at each $x$, so disconnected $X$ requires no choice of a common exponent. If $X$ is empty all sheaf maps are unique. We have linearized $L$ itself; taking $m=1$ gives the stated positive tensor power.

It does not restate the item: there is no action and no cocycle in it. Steps: (1) locnoeth via pqf-def-locnoeth plus the Mathlib leaf 01T6, and T x_S X = X x Spec Z[t^±]; (2) the new node applied to a^*L with ae=1 gives theta_0; (3) End(L)=O(X), and theta=theta_0 q^*(alpha^-1) restricts to 1; (4) the cocycle ratio is a unit d with both face identities; (5) units of R[g^±,h^±] over the domain O_{X,x} are monomials (lexicographic extremal-exponent argument), so the faces force d=1 stalkwise, then coefficientwise on affine U.
